entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Alternative Democratic Pole (Polo Democrático Alternativo, PDA) was a Colombian left-wing political party formed in 2006 through the merger of several Colombian left-wing organizations — representing a significant development in Colombian politics as one of the few successful left-wing parties in a country where leftist political movements had historically been extremely vulnerable to assassination by paramilitary groups associated with Colombia's decades-long armed conflict.

Colombia's political history has been marked by extraordinary political violence against the left: the Unión Patriótica (UP), a leftist party formed in 1985 as part of peace negotiations with the FARC guerrillas, was subjected to systematic assassination — approximately 3,000-5,000 UP members were killed between 1985 and 1993, including presidential candidates, senators, and local officials. This genocide of a political party effectively destroyed the UP and demonstrated the extreme danger of left-wing political participation in Colombia.

The PDA's formation in 2006 thus represented a significant courage: organizing a legal left-wing party in a country where this had historically been a death sentence. The party achieved significant electoral success, winning the Bogotá mayorship (Samuel Moreno, 2007; Gustavo Petro, 2011) and national congressional representation. Gustavo Petro, the most prominent PDA-associated politician, became Colombia's president in 2022 — the first left-wing president in Colombia's history, an extraordinary development given the country's history of left-wing political violence.
